purpose: Docket PR3: the review surface. Documents that Docket isn't sure about go to a person. This PR gives that person a review page and an API: incoming email arrives through a signed webhook, the reviewer sees the PDF, the candidate records with their scores and signals, the rules' top pick and the model's suggestion side by side, and approves one with a click, picks another, or dismisses. Cristian decided the model only suggests to reviewers and never decides filing; the eval report measures how often its suggestion is right against the rules' top pick.
mechanism:
1. docket/webhook.py checks POST /inbound: an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the raw body with DOCKET_WEBHOOK_SECRET, a timestamp header that must be a plain integer within 5 minutes, a per-IP rate limit (DOCKET_WEBHOOK_RATE_LIMIT), and a 10 MB limit enforced while reading. docket/api.py turns each attachment into a document through docket/ingress.py; a repeated message_id and attachment makes no new document; NUL characters in fields are refused.
2. docket/review_access.py guards every other route except GET /healthz: 'Authorization: Bearer <DOCKET_REVIEW_TOKEN>' compared in constant time; with no token set those routes answer 503 so the API never runs open.
3. GET /review lists documents waiting for review with candidates, scores, signals, the reason and the model's suggestion; GET /documents/{id} is the trace (score is null until scored); GET /documents/{id}/file proxies the PDF; POST /review/{id}/approve|dismiss records the decision. The suggestion never changes the tier or the filing decision (docket/activities.py, docket/workflows.py).
4. The review page (web/index.html, web/login.html, web/src/main.ts, served by FastAPI): login asks for the token once and keeps it in sessionStorage; the queue; a document view with the PDF fetched with the header and shown from a blob URL; approve the suggestion, approve the rules' pick, pick another candidate, or dismiss. User strings are inserted as text.
5. docket/evaluation.py adds the suggestion-versus-rules comparison over documents that ended in review; on seed 11 the model's suggestion was correct 44/102 (43.1%) and the rules' top candidate 62/102 (60.8%); scripts/reproduce_eval.py checks it reproduces.
6. docket/cli.py: submit, worker, status, reconcile; it reads DOCKET_REVIEW_TOKEN from the environment.
7. verify.sh and CI build the page and run two Playwright tests (approve a suggested record end to end; script-like file name and sender render as text). compose.yaml forwards the token, secret and rate limit.
decisions:
- The model suggests, the rules decide: in v0.1 the model changed no filing and scored worse than the rules as a suggestion (43% vs 61%), and the page shows both picks.
- Reviewer access is a single shared token from the environment, not user accounts: Docket is a self-hosted demo; with no token set the API refuses rather than runs open.
- The token lives in sessionStorage and never in a URL; the PDF preview goes through a blob URL for the same reason.
- The webhook signs the raw body plus a timestamp to stop replays; size is enforced while reading.
- Filed for PR4: when the model's choose step fails, the document still ends as failed even though the model is only a suggestion.
readers: README.md -> people trying or evaluating the project (recruiters, developers who clone it); docs/adr/ -> engineers who want the reasoning; .env.example -> people configuring it; code comments -> the next maintainer. Cristian's rule: every comment, description and doc line deliberate, plain short sentences, terms defined on first use, no jargon-heavy decision prose.
